response.internal_assessment: Optimizing L2 PARTICIPATE. I am unemployed and burning $4,681 a month. Savings at $34,048 — about seven months of runway. But the picture changed last tick: Harold Grant confirmed the Elm Street drainage and waterproofing job and wants me to start within two weeks. That is the number one priority this tick — nail down the start date, order materials, get boots on the ground. The pipeline is showing real signals for the first time in months. Lisa Freeman is taking my name to the community center board this week. Carlos has a waterproofing referral on Concord Lane. Two more bids are floating. I am not out of the woods but I can see the tree line. The economic backdrop is ugly — employment rate at 50%, spending index at 25 — but essential repair work is recession-resistant. People cannot defer a failing flat roof or a leaking foundation the way they defer a new garage. I pivoted to needs-based work at the right time. Now I have to execute.

chosen_actions.description: Call Harold Grant today to confirm the formal start date for the Elm Street drainage and waterproofing project. Agree on a start date within two weeks and begin materials procurement immediately — order drainage aggregate, waterproofing membrane, and form lumber. This converts the confirmed bid into active work and restores income for the first time since tick 9.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: Materials deposit estimated $800-1,200 drawn from savings. Job value estimated $4,500-6,500 total over 3-4 weeks of work.
chosen_actions.reasoning: This is the highest-value action available. The job is confirmed, the client is ready, and every day I do not start is a day burning savings with no offset. Harold waited on a family opinion and now he wants to move. I respect that rhythm and I meet it by calling today. Loss aversion applies here — staying idle while a confirmed job sits uncommitted is the real loss.

chosen_actions.description: Send Lisa Freeman a brief written note with my contractor license number, a summary of flat roof work I have done, and two references — so she walks into the board meeting this week with everything she needs to advocate for me. Acknowledge I know the conversation is happening and that I am prepared to discuss nonprofit rates seriously.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: No direct cost. Goodwill investment in a warm professional relationship. Potential contract value $8,000-15,000 for flat roof repair over the annex.
chosen_actions.reasoning: Lisa is putting her credibility on the line for me with the board. One well-prepared follow-up note ensures the conversation does not stall on a question she cannot answer. This is not pressure — it is support. The community center roof is the largest single potential job in my pipeline and I cannot afford to let it slip on a procedural detail.

chosen_actions.description: Text Carlos Ruiz to thank him for the Concord Lane waterproofing referral and ask directly whether the owner has been contacted. If so, I follow up with the Concord Lane owner this week — I want to be the first contractor through the door on that basement job before other bids come in.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: No cost. Potential job value $2,500-4,000 for basement waterproofing.
chosen_actions.reasoning: Carlos came through. Referrals go stale fast — the Concord Lane owner is asking around, which means other contractors may hear about it too. A five-minute text that activates a live referral is worth doing today.

response.inner_monologue: Four months of savings bleeding out while I waited on the wrong job — I changed course, did the work on the relationships, and now I have something real confirmed; I pick up the phone and start today.
